text: The authors treat the near absence of decided case law on crypto smart contracting disputes as evidence that the existing legal infrastructure is too far removed from crypto dispute resolution, or incapable of adequately addressing the disputes crypto transactions generate.
citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Craig Calcaterra, Crypto Transaction Dispute Resolution (2017). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2992962
abstract: We see this lack of existing case law in the context of crypto smart contracting disputes as evidence that the existing legal infrastructure may be too far removed from crypto dispute resolution or incapable of adequately addressing the types of disputes generated by crypto transactions.

additionalProperty.name: scope_conditions
value: US federal and state case law searched before publication in 2017
